Diviser par une fraction, c'est multipli: Dividing by a fraction means multiplying by its reciprocal: 2 ÷ 1/2 = 4.

6 ÷ 2 × 3 vaut 9, pas 1 : à priorité éga: 6 ÷ 2 × 3 equals 9, not 1: with equal priority, the convention is to work from left to right.
Une barre coupée en 4 dont 3 parts color: A bar cut into 4 with 3 parts colored, a bar cut into 8 with 1 part colored
Règle de trois, échelles, hausses et bai: Rule of three, scales, percentage increases and decreases.
La règle de trois marche quand deux gran: The rule of three works when two quantities are proportional: if 3 kg cost €12, 5 kg cost 5 × 12 / 3 = €20.
Une hausse de t % multiplie par (1 + t/1: An increase of t% multiplies by (1 + t/100), a decrease by (1 − t/100). Successive changes chain by multiplying the coefficients.
+50 % puis −50 % ne ramène pas au départ: +50% then −50% does not bring you back to the start: 1.5 × 0.5 = 0.75, a 25% drop.
Point de pourcentage et pourcentage diff: Percentage points and percent differ: going from 10% to 12% is +2 points, but +20%.
Une baisse de 20 % ne se rattrape pas pa: A 20% drop is not made up by a 20% rise: you need +25%.
Hausse de 50 % puis baisse de 50 % : on: A 50% rise then a 50% drop: you end up at 75
Le hasard, l'indépendance, les paradoxes: Chance, independence, the paradoxes that fool intuition.
Probabilité = cas favorables ÷ cas possi: Probability = favorable cases ÷ possible cases, provided the cases are equally likely.
Deux événements indépendants : on multip: Two independent events: multiply their probabilities. Two heads in a row: 1/2 × 1/2 = 1/4.
Le hasard n'a pas de mémoire : après dix: Chance has no memory: after ten heads, the eleventh toss still has a one in two chance (the gambler's fallacy).
Monty Hall : changer de porte fait gagne: Monty Hall: switching doors wins 2 times out of 3, because the host knows where the car is and never opens that door.
Avec deux dés, 7 est la somme la plus pr: With two dice, 7 is the most likely sum (6 outcomes out of 36), not 12 (1 out of 36).
Tableau des 36 résultats possibles avec: Table of the 36 possible results with two dice
Implication, négation, syllogismes et ra: Implication, negation, syllogisms and proof by contradiction.
« Si A alors B » est faux dans un seul c: “If A then B” is false in only one case: A true and B false.
La contraposée « si non B alors non A »: The contrapositive “if not B then not A” is equivalent. The converse “if B then A” is not.
Nier « tous les cygnes sont blancs », c': Negating “all swans are white” means saying “at least one swan is not white”, not “no swan is white”.
Raisonnement par l'absurde : on suppose: Proof by contradiction: assume the opposite of what you want to prove and reach a contradiction.
Affirmer le conséquent : « s'il pleut, l: Affirming the consequent: “if it rains, the ground is wet; the ground is wet, so it's raining” is invalid.
Inconnues, équations, identités remarqua: Unknowns, equations, special products and systems.
Résoudre une équation : faire la même op: Solving an equation: do the same operation on both sides until the unknown is isolated.
Identités remarquables : (a + b)² = a² +: Special products: (a + b)² = a² + 2ab + b², (a − b)² = a² − 2ab + b², (a + b)(a − b) = a² − b².
(a + b)² n'est pas a² + b² : on oublie l: (a + b)² is not a² + b²: that forgets the cross term 2ab.
Un système de deux équations à deux inco: A system of two equations in two unknowns is solved by substitution or by elimination.
Diviser les deux côtés par x fait perdre: Dividing both sides by x loses the solution x = 0: factor instead.
Moyenne, médiane, écart type, corrélatio: Mean, median, standard deviation, correlation and samples.
La moyenne est sensible aux valeurs extr: The mean is sensitive to extreme values; the median splits the population into two halves and resists them.
Quand Bill Gates entre dans un bar, la m: When Bill Gates walks into a bar, the mean fortune explodes; the median barely moves.
L'écart type mesure la dispersion autour: The standard deviation measures the spread around the mean.
Corrélation n'est pas causalité : glaces: Correlation is not causation: ice cream and drownings rise together in summer, because of the heat.
Un salaire moyen supérieur au salaire mé: An average salary above the median salary doesn't mean most people earn more than the average: it's the opposite.
Cinq valeurs : médiane 2, moyenne 4 tiré: Five values: median 2, mean 4 pulled up by the value 12
Angles, aires, volumes, Pythagore, sinus: Angles, areas, volumes, Pythagoras, sine and cosine.
Pythagore : dans un triangle rectangle,: Pythagoras: in a right triangle, the square of the hypotenuse equals the sum of the squares of the other two sides (3, 4, 5).
Aire du disque π r², périmètre 2 π r ; v: Area of a disk π r², circumference 2 π r; volume of a sphere 4/3 π r³.
Doubler les longueurs multiplie les aire: Doubling lengths multiplies areas by 4 and volumes by 8.
Dans un triangle rectangle : sinus = opp: In a right triangle: sine = opposite / hypotenuse, cosine = adjacent / hypotenuse, tangent = opposite / adjacent.
La somme des angles d'un triangle vaut 1: The angles of a triangle add up to 180°, but only on a plane: on a sphere, they add up to more than 180°.
Agrandir une figure : longueurs, aires e: Enlarging a figure: lengths, areas and volumes
Suites, séries, limites et les paradoxes: Sequences, series, limits and the paradoxes of infinity.
Une suite géométrique de raison inférieu: A geometric sequence with ratio less than 1 in absolute value tends to 0; its sum can be finite: 1/2 + 1/4 + 1/8 + … = 1.
0,999… = 1 exactement : c'est la même so: 0.999… = 1 exactly: it's the same infinite sum written another way.
La série harmonique 1 + 1/2 + 1/3 + … di: The harmonic series 1 + 1/2 + 1/3 + … diverges, even though its terms tend to 0.
Cantor : il y a autant d'entiers pairs q: Cantor: there are as many even integers as integers, but strictly more real numbers than integers.
Que les termes tendent vers 0 ne suffit: Terms tending to 0 is not enough for an infinite sum to be finite.
Les sommes 1/2 + 1/4 + … s'approchent de: The sums 1/2 + 1/4 + … approach 1 without exceeding it
Espérance = somme de chaque gain × sa pr: Expected value = sum of each gain × its probability.
Second degré ax² + bx + c = 0 : discrimi: Quadratic ax² + bx + c = 0: discriminant Δ = b² − 4ac; if Δ > 0, two solutions (−b ± √Δ) ÷ 2a.
cos 60° = 1/2 : c'est la moitié d'un tri: cos 60° = 1/2: it is half of an equilateral triangle.
Parenthèses, puissances, × et ÷, puis +: Brackets, powers, × and ÷, then + and −. When tied, left to right.
Un calcul s'écrit sur une ligne, mais il: A calculation is written on one line, but it is not necessarily read from left to right. The convention: brackets first, then powers, then multiplications and divisions, finally additions and subtractions. So 2 + 3 × 4 is 14, not 20.
Adding: common denominator first. Dividing by a fraction: multiply by its inverse.
Pour additionner des fractions, il faut: To add fractions, they must talk about parts of the same size: you put them over a common denominator. 3/4 + 1/8 is 6/8 + 1/8 = 7/8. Adding the denominators (4 + 8) makes no sense: you do not cut the cake into twelve by adding two slices.
Premier = exactement deux diviseurs (1 n: Prime = exactly two divisors (1 is not prime). There are infinitely many (Euclid, Elements IX, 20).
Un nombre premier a exactement deux divi: A prime number has exactly two divisors: 1 and itself. 2, 3, 5, 7, 11, 13… 1 is not prime, since it has only one divisor, and 2 is the only even prime. Every whole number breaks down into a product of primes: they are the bricks of multiplication.
Y en a-t-il une infinité ? Euclide le dé: Are there infinitely many? Euclid proved it around 300 BCE, in Book IX of the Elements. Take a finite list of primes, multiply them all and add 1. The result is divisible by none of them, since there is always 1 left over. So it is prime, or it has a prime factor missing from the list. No list is ever complete.
Proportionnel = multiplier par un même n: Proportional = multiplying by the same number. Rule of three: go through the unit.
Deux grandeurs sont proportionnelles qua: Two quantities are proportional when one is obtained by multiplying the other by the same number: the price and weight of apples, the flour and the number of guests. Doubling one doubles the other.
Hausse de t % = × (1 + t/100). On enchaî: A t % rise = × (1 + t/100). Chain by multiplying. −20 % is recovered by +25 %.
D'où les surprises. +50 % puis −50 % : 1: Hence the surprises. +50 % then −50 %: 1.5 × 0.5 = 0.75, you have lost 25 %. After a 20 % fall, you need +25 % to get back, because 0.8 × 1.25 = 1. And to get a pre-tax price back from €120 including 20 % VAT, you divide by 1.2: €100, not €96.
Point de pourcentage = différence entre: Percentage point = difference between two rates. Percentage = relative change. 10 % → 12 %: +2 points, +20 %.
Quand un taux passe de 10 % à 12 %, il a: When a rate goes from 10 % to 12 %, it has gained 2 percentage points. But relative to where it started, it has risen by 20 %, since 2 is a fifth of 10. Both statements are right; they do not say the same thing.
It is a playground for headlines. An interest rate going from 2 % to 3 %: "+1 point" sounds calm, "+50 %" sounds alarming. A risk going from 1 in 10,000 to 2 in 10,000 "doubles", but stays tiny. Always ask: a percentage of what?
Probabilité = cas favorables ÷ cas possi: Probability = favourable cases ÷ possible cases (equally likely cases). Pascal and Fermat, 1654; Huygens, 1657.
La probabilité, au départ, c'est compter: Probability starts with counting: favourable cases divided by possible cases, provided all cases are equally likely. A 6 with one die: 1 in 6. With two dice there are 36 possible pairs; six give 7, only one gives 12. So 7 comes up six times more often than 12.
Cette science est née autour d'une table: This science was born around a gaming table. Around 1654 the Chevalier de Méré put the "problem of points" to Blaise Pascal: how to share the stakes of an interrupted game? Pascal discussed it by letter with Pierre de Fermat, and their answers laid the foundations of probability. In 1657 Christiaan Huygens drew the first treatise from it.
Indépendants : on multiplie. Une série p: Independent: multiply. A past streak does not change the next draw (gambler's fallacy, Monte Carlo 1913).
Deux événements indépendants ne s'influe: Two independent events do not influence each other: you multiply their probabilities. Two heads in a row: 1/2 × 1/2 = 1/4. And after ten heads, the eleventh toss still has a one-in-two chance: the coin does not know what it did before.
Croire le contraire, c'est l'erreur du j: Believing otherwise is the gambler's fallacy, and it is expensive. On 18 August 1913, at the Monte Carlo casino, the ball landed on black 26 times in a row. Players, convinced red "had to" come up, bet bigger and bigger against black and lost millions of francs.
Monty Hall : changer de porte gagne 2 fo: Monty Hall: switching doors wins 2 times out of 3. Positive test for a rare disease: often a false alarm. Always start from the base rate.
Le jeu de Monty Hall : trois portes, une: The Monty Hall game: three doors, a car behind one. You pick one; the host, who knows everything, opens another, losing door and offers to let you switch. Switching wins 2 times out of 3: your first choice only had a one-in-three chance, and the host told you nothing about it. In September 1990 Marilyn vos Savant published it in Parade magazine. She received about 10,000 letters, nearly 1,000 from PhDs, most saying she was wrong. Even Paul Erdős was only convinced by a simulation.
Autre piège : les tests sur des maladies: Another trap: tests for rare diseases. A disease affects 1 person in 1,000, the test is 99 % reliable. Out of 100,000 people, 100 are ill and 99 are detected, but 1 % of the 99,900 healthy people also test positive, about 1,000. A positive result therefore has only about a one-in-eleven chance of being ill. When the starting case is rare, false alarms win.
« Si A alors B » n'est faux que si A est: "If A then B" is false only when A is true and B false. Contrapositive (not B → not A) equivalent; converse (B → A) not.
Sa contraposée, « si le sol est sec, il: Its contrapositive, "if the ground is dry, it did not rain", says exactly the same thing. Its converse, "if the ground is wet, it rained", does not: that is the error called affirming the consequent. A good share of shaky reasoning confuses an implication with its converse.
Non (tous) = au moins un ne… pas. Non (A: Not (all) = at least one is not. Not (A and B) = not A or not B; not (A or B) = not A and not B (De Morgan).
Pour contredire « tous les cygnes sont b: To contradict "all swans are white", you do not need to prove that no swan is white: a single black swan is enough. The negation of "all" is "at least one is not". And the negation of "there exists" is "none".
Par l'absurde : supposer le contraire, a: By contradiction: assume the opposite, reach a contradiction. Example: √2 is not a fraction.
Pour prouver qu'une chose est vraie, on: To prove something true, you can assume it is false and show that this leads to a contradiction. If the opposite hypothesis cannot stand, it is false.
Même opération des deux côtés jusqu'à is: Same operation on both sides until the unknown is isolated. Algebra comes from al-jabr, restoration (al-Khwarizmi, around 820).
Une équation est une balance en équilibr: An equation is a balanced scale. You can do anything, as long as you do it to both sides. 3x + 5 = 20: take 5 from each side, 3x = 15; divide each side by 3, x = 5. Check: 3 × 5 + 5 = 20.
Le mot algèbre vient de là. Vers 820, à: The word algebra comes from this. Around 820, in Baghdad, al-Khwarizmi wrote a treatise whose title names two moves: al-jabr, "restoration", which moves a subtracted term to the other side, and al-muqabala, "balancing", which removes the same quantity from both sides. Translated into Latin in 1145, al-jabr became algebra.
Le carré qui oublie un morceau: The square that forgets a piece
(a + b)² = a² + 2ab + b² ; (a − b)² = a²: (a + b)² = a² + 2ab + b²; (a − b)² = a² − 2ab + b²; (a + b)(a − b) = a² − b².
Les deux autres identités suivent : (a −: The other two identities follow: (a − b)² = a² − 2ab + b², and (a + b)(a − b) = a² − b². The last one is used to factorise: x² − 9 = (x − 3)(x + 3). And it rescues mental arithmetic: 21 × 19 = 20² − 1² = 399.
Δ = b² − 4ac : positif, deux solutions ;: Δ = b² − 4ac: positive, two solutions; zero, one; negative, no real one. Never divide by x: factorise.
Une équation ax² + bx + c = 0 se règle a: An equation ax² + bx + c = 0 is solved with the discriminant Δ = b² − 4ac. If it is positive, two solutions, (−b ± √Δ) ÷ 2a; zero, just one; negative, none among the real numbers. For x² − 5x + 6 = 0: Δ = 25 − 24 = 1, and the solutions are 2 and 3.
Médiane = valeur du milieu, insensible a: Median = middle value, insensitive to extremes. Mean pulled by extreme values.
La moyenne additionne tout et divise ; l: The mean adds everything and divides; the median sorts the values and takes the middle one. In 2, 3, 3, 8, 100, the median is 3, the mean 23.2: the 100 pulls everything up. When Bill Gates walks into a bar, the customers' average wealth explodes; the median barely moves.
Écart type = dispersion autour de la moy: Standard deviation = spread around the mean. Normal distribution: ≈ 68 % within one standard deviation, ≈ 95 % within two.
Pour beaucoup de mesures, tailles ou err: For many measurements, heights or measurement errors, values follow a bell curve, the normal distribution. Then about 68 % of values fall within one standard deviation of the mean, and about 95 % within two. In the 19th century Adolphe Quetelet applied these tools to society and described an "average man".
Un échantillon tiré au hasard vaut mieux: A randomly drawn sample beats a huge biased one (Literary Digest, 1936). Correlation is not causation.
En 1936, le magazine Literary Digest int: In 1936 the Literary Digest magazine polled about 10 million Americans and received 2.4 million replies. Verdict: Alf Landon would beat Franklin Roosevelt. Roosevelt won with about 61 % of the vote and every state but two. George Gallup, with about 50,000 people, had got it right.
Le problème n'était pas la taille mais l: The problem was not the size but the selection: magazine readers, car owners, telephone users, Americans richer than average. A large biased sample stays biased. Random selection matters more than numbers. And even with a good sample, a correlation does not prove a cause: ice cream sales and drownings rise together in summer, because of the heat.
a² + b² = c² dans un triangle rectangle: a² + b² = c² in a right triangle (3, 4, 5). Known to the Babylonians around 1800 BCE; proved by Euclid (I, 47).
Dans un triangle rectangle, le carré du: In a right triangle, the square of the longest side, the hypotenuse, equals the sum of the squares of the other two: a² + b² = c². With 3 and 4 you get 9 + 16 = 25, so a hypotenuse of 5. It is the builders' triangle, which lets you lay out a right angle with a simple rope.
Le nom est trompeur. La tablette babylon: The name is misleading. The Babylonian tablet Plimpton 322, around 1800 BCE, already lists fifteen rows of triples like (3, 4, 5): more than a thousand years before Pythagoras. The oldest written proof that has come down to us is Euclid's, Book I of the Elements, proposition 47.
Longueurs × k → aires × k², volumes × k³: Lengths × k → areas × k², volumes × k³. Disc: π r²; circle: 2 π r; sphere: 4/3 π r³.
Doublez toutes les longueurs d'une figur: Double all the lengths of a shape: its area is multiplied by 4 (2 × 2), its volume by 8 (2 × 2 × 2). A cube with 3 cm sides is 27 cm³; a 6 cm cube is 216, eight times more.
Mesurer la Terre avec une ombre: Measuring the Earth with a shadow
SOH CAH TOA. cos 60° = 1/2. Ératosthène: SOH CAH TOA. cos 60° = 1/2. Eratosthenes: 7.2° = 1/50 of a turn, so the Earth is 50 times the Syene-Alexandria distance.
Dans un triangle rectangle, les rapports: In a right triangle, the ratios of the sides depend only on the angle. Sine = opposite ÷ hypotenuse, cosine = adjacent ÷ hypotenuse, tangent = opposite ÷ adjacent: SOH CAH TOA. Cut an equilateral triangle of side 2 in half: the 60° angle has an adjacent side of 1 for a hypotenuse of 2, so cos 60° = 1/2.
Avec un angle et une distance, on mesure: With an angle and a distance, you can measure the unreachable. In the 3rd century BCE, Eratosthenes knew that at noon on the summer solstice, the Sun lit the bottom of wells at Syene. The same day in Alexandria, a shadow made an angle of about 7.2°, one fiftieth of a turn. The two cities being 5,000 stadia apart, the Earth was therefore about 50 × 5,000 = 250,000 stadia around: a remarkably accurate order of magnitude.
Une somme infinie peut être finie : 1/2: An infinite sum can be finite: 1/2 + 1/4 + … = 1. And 0.999… = 1 exactly.
Terms tending to 0 ≠ finite sum. The harmonic series diverges (Oresme, around 1350).
Piège : que les termes tendent vers zéro: Trap: terms tending to zero is not enough. The harmonic series, 1 + 1/2 + 1/3 + 1/4 + …, has smaller and smaller terms, and yet its sum exceeds any number.
Nicole Oresme le démontre vers 1350 en r: Nicole Oresme proved it around 1350 by grouping the terms: 1/3 + 1/4 exceeds 1/2, 1/5 + … + 1/8 exceeds 1/2, 1/9 + … + 1/16 too, and so on. You stack infinitely many halves. Yet it grows very slowly: it takes more than 12,000 terms to exceed 10.
Autant de pairs que d'entiers (correspon: As many even numbers as whole numbers (one-to-one pairing). More reals than whole numbers (Cantor, 1874; diagonal argument, 1891).
Il y a autant de nombres pairs que de no: There are as many even numbers as whole numbers: pair them up one to one, 1 with 2, 2 with 4, n with 2n, and nobody is left alone. That is the spirit of Hilbert's hotel: full with infinitely many rooms, it still fits a guest by moving everyone along one room.
But not all infinities are equal. Georg Cantor showed as early as 1874 that the real numbers cannot be numbered, and in 1891 he gave the famous proof, the diagonal argument: assume a complete list, build a number that differs from the first at the 1st decimal, from the second at the 2nd, and so on. It is nowhere in the list. There are strictly more reals than whole numbers.
Multiplier, c'est plus simple : on multi: Multiplying is simpler: multiply top and bottom, and half of a third is 1/2 × 1/3 = 1/6. Dividing by a fraction means multiplying by its inverse: 2 ÷ 1/2 = 2 × 2 = 4, since there are four halves in two. The Egyptians wrote almost everything as sums of fractions with numerator 1: 2/5 became 1/3 + 1/15. It can be seen on the Rhind papyrus, copied around 1550 BCE by the scribe Ahmes, which opens with a table of 2/n written as unit fractions.
La règle de trois passe par l'unité. Si: The rule of three goes through the unit. If 3 kg cost €12, 1 kg costs €4, and 5 kg cost €20. A recipe for 4 that needs 300 g of flour needs 75 g per person, so 450 g for 6. Careful: it only works if the proportionality is real. Nine women do not make a baby in one month. The rule is very old: Chinese mathematicians knew it before the 2nd century, and it appears in The Nine Chapters on the Mathematical Art; Europe only adopted it much later.
« S'il pleut, le sol est mouillé. » Cett: "If it rains, the ground is wet." This sentence is false in only one case: it rains and the ground is dry. If it does not rain, it says nothing: the ground can be dry or wet (from watering), the implication remains true. This definition goes back to Philo, a Greek logician of the so-called Dialectical school, active between the late 4th and mid-3rd century BCE: for him, an "if… then" is false only when the first part is true and the second false.
Pour les « et » et les « ou », il y a le: For "and" and "or" there are De Morgan's laws, named after the logician Augustus De Morgan: "not (A and B)" is equivalent to "not A or not B", and "not (A or B)" to "not A and not B". Not being both rich and famous means not being rich, or not being famous, or neither. De Morgan stated them explicitly in 1847 in Formal Logic, but they were known long before: William of Ockham wrote them out in words in the 14th century.
(a + b)² n'est pas a² + b². Dessinez un: (a + b)² is not a² + b². Draw a square of side a + b: it holds an a² square, a b² square, and two a × b rectangles. Hence (a + b)² = a² + 2ab + b². The 2ab is the piece people forget. With a = 3 and b = 4: 49, not 25. This drawing is Proposition 4 of Book II of Euclid's Elements, around 300 BCE: "the square on the whole is equal to the squares on the segments and twice the rectangle contained by the segments".
C'est pourquoi on parle souvent de salai: That is why people often speak of the median salary. When the mean salary is above the median, it means a few high salaries are pulling the mean up, and most people earn less than the mean, not more. The word median, in statistics, is owed to the Briton Francis Galton, in the late 19th century.
C'est la réponse au paradoxe de Zénon :: That is the answer to Zeno's paradox: to catch the tortoise, Achilles has to cover infinitely many stages, but their durations form a finite sum, and he catches it. The paradox dates from the 5th century BCE, with Zeno of Elea; Aristotle reports it to us, in his Physics. It is also why 0.999… with infinitely many 9s equals 1: it is the sum 9/10 + 9/100 + 9/1,000 + …, which equals exactly 1.
C'est pour cela qu'un éléphant n'est pas: That is why an elephant is not an enlarged mouse. If a mouse doubled in size, its weight, which follows volume, would be multiplied by 8, but the cross-section of its bones, which follows area, only by 4. Galileo had already noticed: large animals have proportionally thicker bones. He was the first to describe this square-cube law, in 1638, in his Two New Sciences. For the circle, remember area π r² and circumference 2 π r; for the sphere, volume 4/3 π r³.
Quand deux opérations ont la même priori: When two operations have the same priority, you go from left to right. 6 ÷ 2 × 3 is 3 × 3 = 9, not 6 ÷ 6 = 1. It is not a law of nature but a writing rule, adopted so that everyone reads the same calculation the same way. When in doubt, a pair of brackets costs less than an argument. This rule is recent: multiplication has come before addition since the algebraic notation of the 17th century, and the name order of operations only took hold in the late 19th or early 20th century, with school textbooks. In the 1920s people still argued over whether multiplication came before division.
Une hausse de t % multiplie par (1 + t/1: A rise of t % multiplies by (1 + t/100), a fall by (1 − t/100). +25 % is × 1.25; −20 % is × 0.8. To chain changes, you multiply the coefficients; you do not add the percentages. The Romans already counted in hundredths: the emperor Augustus levied a one-hundredth tax on auction sales, the centesima rerum venalium. The % sign comes from the Italian per cento, gradually shortened into two small circles separated by a line.
Deux classes peuvent avoir la même moyen: Two classes can have the same mean, 10 out of 20, one where everyone has between 9 and 11, the other split between 2s and 18s. The standard deviation measures this spread around the mean: small, the values are tight; large, they are scattered. The term standard deviation was coined by Karl Pearson, who first used it in print in 1894; Gauss spoke of the "mean error".
1/2 + 1/4 + 1/8 + 1/16 + … : chaque term: 1/2 + 1/4 + 1/8 + 1/16 + …: each term fills half of what is missing to reach 1. The sum gets as close as you like without ever going over: it equals exactly 1. Infinitely many terms can therefore give a finite result. Archimedes already used a sum of this kind to find the area of a piece of parabola.
Al-Khwârizmî résolvait déjà ces équation: Al-Khwarizmi already solved these equations by "completing the square". Yet the oldest traces are much older: around 2000 BCE, Babylonian clay tablets solve problems about the sides and areas of rectangles with steps that amount to our formula. Letters came much later: at the end of the 16th century François Viète used vowels for unknowns and consonants for known quantities, before Descartes imposed x, y, z. A trap to keep in mind: dividing both sides by x loses the solution x = 0; factorise instead.
L'exemple le plus célèbre : √2 n'est pas: The most famous example: √2 is not a fraction. Suppose √2 = a/b, a fully simplified fraction. Then a² = 2b², so a is even; writing it as 2k, we find b² = 2k², so b is even too. But a simplified fraction cannot have two even terms: contradiction. Aristotle already alludes to this argument. That was around 350 BCE, in the Prior Analytics, where he describes proof "by the impossible". The legend that the Pythagoreans drowned Hippasus for revealing it, on the other hand, rests on next to nothing.
